title: Address Poisoning: The Copy-Paste Trick That Can Empty a Crypto Wallet
caption: Educational only. Not financial advice. Address poisoning is when scammers send tiny transfers from a look-alike wallet address, hoping you copy it later by mistake. Sources: MetaMask Support, Trust Wallet, Elliptic, Bitdefender. AI-generated voice. Educational only. Not financial advice.

scenes.head: COPY-PASTE TRAP
scenes.narration: Would you notice if one crypto address was almost the same as yours? Scammers count on you not noticing.

scenes.head: WHAT IT IS
scenes.narration: Address poisoning is when a scammer makes a look-alike address and sends you a tiny transfer so it shows in your history.

scenes.head: THE TRICK
scenes.narration: The fake address often matches the first and last few characters of one you really use, so it looks familiar.

scenes.head: THE MISTAKE
scenes.narration: Later, you copy an address from your history, send money, and it lands with the scammer. Transfers cannot be reversed.

scenes.head: HOW TO STAY SAFE
scenes.narration: Check every character, not just the start and end. Avoid copying from your history, and consider a small test transfer first.

scenes.head: MORE HABITS
scenes.narration: Save trusted addresses in your wallet, ignore random tiny deposits, and never interact with tokens you did not ask for.

scenes.head: EDUCATION, NOT ADVICE
scenes.narration: A few extra seconds of checking can protect your funds. This is education, not advice.
